research_summary: Spec section 4.2 (Unit R050) was cross-referenced against the existing 8 lessons. The Jan 2025 OCR examiner's report explicitly flags four under-performed exam questions whose content is NOT meaningfully addressed by L1-L8: Q11 (types of interactivity), Q13(c) hardware resources for HCI/TA2.2 ('many candidates did not gain any marks'), Q18(a) email distribution channel advantages where candidates 'described what email is rather than the advantages', and the spec area 5.5 audience demographics which is exam-tested but absent from L1-L8. Two further whitelisted sources confirmed: the OCR R050 understanding-the-exam blog post (which highlights synoptic application of TA2 software/hardware considerations) and the J836 specification version 6 (Sept 2025) itself.

rejected_candidates.cloud_models_saas_paas_iaas: Not in J836 R050 spec. Cloud appears only as a storage location (3.4) and distribution channel (5.4.1) — SaaS/PaaS/IaaS is OCR Computer Science J277 territory, not Cambridge Nationals IT.
rejected_candidates.mobile_technologies_apps_discrete: Already covered in L7 via TA5 (mobile apps as distribution channel) and TA5.4.2 connectivity (4G/5G, mobile Wi-Fi hotspots). Adding it would overlap.
rejected_candidates.accessibility_inclusive_design_wcag_rsi: WCAG and RSI are not in the J836 spec. The spec only lists 'accessibility' as one of four audience demographics in 5.5. Folded into Lesson 11 (audience demographics).
rejected_candidates.file_types_compression_conversion: Not in J836 R050 spec. Belongs to OCR Computer Science J277.
rejected_candidates.authentication_methods_deep_dive: Already covered in L6 (TA4.3 prevention measures: 2FA, biometrics, usernames and passwords).
rejected_candidates.data_interpretation_presentation_charts: Not a discrete spec topic. L1 covers visualisation diagrams.
rejected_candidates.lan_wan_pan_vpn_networking: Network topology terminology (LAN/WAN/PAN/VPN) is not in the J836 R050 spec. Spec only requires connectivity methods (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, wired, 4G/5G, mobile hotspots) which L7 covers.
rejected_candidates.backups_redundancy_disaster_recovery: Already covered in L6 (TA4.3 secure backups; Q17(a) of Jan 2025 paper tested this).
rejected_candidates.health_safety_in_it_use: Health and Safety at Work Act is in spec 4.4 only as legislation; spec explicitly says 'Does not include: Detailed knowledge of the legislations'. RSI/posture/electrical safety are not required and would not earn marks. Already covered in L6 legislation.

new_lessons.title: Hardware Considerations for Designing Interfaces
new_lessons.description: Display type, screen size, memory and processing power — and how each shapes the design of an HCI.
new_lessons.rationale: Examiner Jan 2025 Q13(c) verbatim: 'Many candidates did not gain any marks on this question' on hardware resources for HCI; examiner explicitly flags 'confusion between memory and storage'. L2 (HCI in Everyday Life) addresses purpose and application areas (TA2.1) but the spec's TA2.2 hardware sub-topic — display type/size, memory, processing power and their *impact on the HCI* — is its own examined sub-section. Worth a discrete lesson because exam questions test it as a stand-alone analysis skill ('select hardware for this scenario').
key_topics: Display type (LCD, OLED, e-ink, capacitive touch) and impact on HCI design
Display size (smartwatch vs phone vs laptop vs smartboard) and layout consequences
Memory (RAM) vs storage — fundamental distinction examiner explicitly flagged
Processing power and its effect on HCI responsiveness, animations, real-time features
Advantages and disadvantages of hardware resource choices
Selecting suitable hardware for a given context (banking app on phone vs retail till)

new_lessons.title: Operating Systems and Digital Platforms
new_lessons.description: How Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, Chrome, Linux and Unix shape interface design — and the digital platforms they run.
new_lessons.rationale: Spec TA2.3 lists eight operating systems by name (Windows, Apple macOS, Apple iOS, Android, Chrome, Ubuntu, Linux, Unix) plus four digital platform types (database, mobile app, spreadsheet, website) and requires knowledge of how each impacts HCI design. L2 covers HCI application areas, not the operating system layer. This is heavy-content under-taught territory: the examiner blog explicitly says 'R050 contains content that is not covered in the NEA units which needs to be taught and revised fully'.
key_topics: What an operating system does (manages hardware, provides HCI, runs software)
Desktop OSs: Windows, macOS, Ubuntu/Linux/Unix, Chrome — comparison and use cases
Mobile OSs: iOS vs Android — closed vs open ecosystem, app store control
Embedded OSs (smart TV, smartwatch, IoE device firmware)
How OS choice impacts HCI design (gestures on iOS, taskbar on Windows, terminal on Linux)
Digital platforms: database, mobile app, spreadsheet, website
How each platform shapes what the HCI looks like and how users interact with it

new_lessons.title: Choosing Devices and Distribution Channels for an Audience
new_lessons.description: Smartphones, tablets, smartboards and PCs matched to audience age, location and accessibility needs.
new_lessons.rationale: Spec 5.3 (smartphone, smart TV, PC/laptop, tablet, smartboard) and 5.5 (audience demographics: accessibility, age, gender, location) are explicit teaching content. Jan 2025 Q18(a) email-advantages question: 'Most candidates did not gain any marks... candidates described what email is rather than the advantages of using it'. The audience-justification skill is exactly what Section B scenarios test ('Recommend a device and channel for X audience'). L7 likely focused on connectivity (5.4.2) and types (5.1); the *device-and-audience justification* layer is its own exam-tested decision-making skill.
key_topics: Digital device characteristics: smartphone, smart TV, PC/laptop, tablet, smartboard
When each device is and is not suitable (boardroom presentation vs coffee shop survey)
Audience demographics: accessibility (motor, visual, hearing, cognitive)
Audience demographics: age (children, working adults, older adults)
Audience demographics: gender and location (cultural, regional, urban vs rural broadband)
Linking the digital communication, distribution channel and connectivity to the demographic
Worked exam-style scenario: matching a device + channel + connectivity to a target audience

new_lessons.title: User Interaction Methods and Digital Interactivity
new_lessons.description: Gesture, voice, touch, mouse and keyboard — plus how devices and humans interact in the connected world.
new_lessons.rationale: Spec 2.4 (gesture, keyboard, mouse, touch, voice) and 6.1 (IoE digital interactivity: device-to-device, human-to-device, tailoring devices to user needs) sit across two topic areas but cover the same conceptual skill: how users and devices communicate. Jan 2025 Q11 examiner verbatim: 'This question was not well answered, this is despite the types of interactivity being listed in the specification content.' L2 and L8 likely brushed past these as sub-bullets; this lesson treats them as the central topic with worked advantages/disadvantages of each method.
key_topics: Five user interaction methods: gesture, keyboard, mouse, touch, voice
Advantages and disadvantages of each method (speed, accuracy, accessibility, hygiene)
Suitability for different contexts (ATM touch vs hands-free voice in a kitchen)
Device-to-device interactivity (smart bulb to hub, fitness band to phone, car to satnav)
Human-to-device interactivity in the IoE
How devices can be tailored to meet end-user needs (large text mode, voice access, haptic feedback)
Why the wrong interaction method costs marks in exam scenarios
